evidence.quote: today the Federal Open Market Committee decided to lower our policy interest rate by ¼ percentage point.
This path is ¼ percentage point lower than projected in June.
With downside risks to employment having increased, the balance of risks has shifted.
we see that the labor market is softening, and we don't need it to soften any more, don't want it to.
Our obligation is to ensure that a one-time increase in the price level does not become an ongoing inflation problem.
We also decided to continue to reduce our securities holdings.

parsed.rationale: The Chair announces a 25bp risk-management cut and a lower SEP rate path, citing a softening labor market and rising downside employment risks, while noting elevated tariff-driven inflation. He frames further moves as heading toward neutral on a meeting-by-meeting basis, rejecting the idea of larger cuts.
